title: SOP: intake for customer audit log export requests
content:
> **Archived 2025-02-03:** this page is superseded by "SOP: intake and coordination for customer-managed audit log export requests" and is kept for reference only.

# Purpose
How Customer Success (CS) and Support take in, scope and coordinate requests from customers who want Redwood audit logs exported to storage they manage, for Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments.

# When to use
- A customer wants Redwood audit logs delivered to their cloud storage or SIEM.
- A security questionnaire asks how audit logs are delivered and the customer wants automated export.

# Request intake checklist (CS/Support)
Record the following on the Jira ticket:
- Customer company
- Deployment mode: Hosted | Dedicated | Private
- Regions in use
- Desired sink: S3 | GCS | Azure Blob
- Destination: bucket/container name, prefix, destination region
- Identity method: AWS assume-role / IRSA, GCP workload identity, or Azure workload identity
- Retention intent (owned by the customer)
- Operational and escalation contacts
- Target date, if an audit depends on it

# Handoff and approvals
## 1) Open the Jira ticket
- Project: cs-escalations
- Issue type: Support Request
- Priority:
  - P2 for standard requests
  - P1 if a customer audit deadline falls within 30 days
  - P0 only when it blocks a live incident response obligation

## 2) Security approval
- Assign a Security reviewer and request approval following the Security controls page.
- Attach the destination policy snippets and confirmation of encryption.

## 3) Legal/Privacy approval (when needed)
Escalate to Legal/Privacy for cross-region export, PII fields beyond the standard audit schema, or contracts with custom data residency clauses.

# Execution routing
Once approved:
- Hosted: Eng Platform oncall / platform ops
- Dedicated: Eng Infra
- Private: Private Deployments engineering, together with the customer's operator

# Customer communication template (email)
Subject: Audit log export enablement – next steps

Body:
- Thank you for your request. We can set up automated export of Redwood platform audit logs to your [S3/GCS/Azure] destination.
- Please confirm the destination bucket/container exists and has encryption at rest enabled.
- Please send the workload identity / role configuration using the attached template.
- After approval we will turn on export and ask you to confirm objects appear under the agreed prefix.
- Typical initial enablement time: 5–10 business days, depending on deployment mode and approvals.

# Validation responsibilities
- Redwood: checks connector health metrics and the first delivery to the destination.
- Customer: checks SIEM ingestion and sets up their own retention and alerts.

# Post-enablement notes
- Make sure the customer understands delivery is at-least-once and duplicates are possible.
- Remind the customer that the destination, its storage cost and lifecycle policies are theirs.
